NDT training in Iowa: how it works for Iowa employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training in Iowa is delivered by Atlantis NDT under the ASNT SNT-TC-1A model, either live online or onsite at your own facility in Des Moines, Cedar Rapids, the Quad Cities, Sioux City, Waterloo, Council Bluffs or anywhere else in the state. Classroom hours come from us; on-the-job experience, exams and certification are recorded under your employer's written practice, with an ASNT Level III administering the exams. Quotes are returned within one business day.

Iowa is not a coastal refinery market, and that changes what NDT training has to look like here. The work is spread across a wide state: heavy-equipment and agricultural machinery plants, ethanol and biodiesel facilities, wind-energy supply chains, coal and gas generating stations, interstate pipelines, grain-handling structures and a very large inventory of state and county bridges. A technician in Sioux City may spend a week on pressure vessels at a processing plant, then move to structural welds on a steel fabrication job. That mix is why Iowa employers tend to value technicians who hold more than one method, and why onsite or online delivery usually makes more sense than sending a crew out of state for a week.

Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in Iowa or anywhere else. We bring the course to you: live-virtual classroom sessions for theory, and onsite sessions at your shop or plant for hands-on work on your own specimens and equipment, all under ASNT Level III oversight. If you run a small inspection company in Cedar Rapids with three technicians, or a manufacturing QA department in Waterloo that needs its first in-house MT and PT Level IIs, the model is the same: we fit the training to your written practice rather than asking you to fit your people to a fixed campus timetable.

Request an Iowa training quote and tell us the methods, levels and number of people involved.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Iowa

Every course below is structured around the ASNT SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge and the recommended topical outlines in ANSI/ASNT CP-105. Level I and II courses cover theory, equipment, calibration, technique, code interpretation and reporting; Level III preparation covers the method in depth plus the basic examination topics (materials, processes, other methods and SNT-TC-1A itself). The table shows how each method maps to work Iowa employers actually do.

MethodLevelsWhat Iowa employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepWeld inspection on structural steel and bridge girders to AWS D1.1 and D1.5, thickness surveys on ethanol plant piping and tanks, lamination checks on plate at fabrication shopsLevel I: none beyond employer entry requirements. Level II: Level I training plus experience per your written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, IIWeld examination on pressure vessels and pipe, corrosion mapping on process equipment, advanced inspection where RT is impractical inside a running plantConventional UT Level II strongly recommended
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, IIFlaw sizing on thick-wall vessel and pipe welds, often paired with PAUT on fabrication and repair workConventional UT Level II strongly recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline girth welds to API 1104, vessel and piping welds to ASME Section VIII and B31.3, casting evaluation at foundriesSeparate state radiation safety training and certification required before handling sources (see below)
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepSurface crack detection on welded frames, booms, axles and forgings in equipment manufacturing; weld inspection on structural and bridge steelNone beyond employer entry requirements
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepStainless and aluminium welds in food, ethanol and processing plants; non-magnetic castings; component inspection at manufacturersNone beyond employer entry requirements
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual inspection on every fabrication job, bridge and structural inspections, pre- and post-repair checks during plant outagesNone beyond employer entry requirements
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, IIHeat exchanger and condenser tube inspection at generating stations and process plants, surface crack detection on components and coatingsNone beyond employer entry requirements

A practical pattern we see in Iowa manufacturing is VT, MT and PT first, because they cover the bulk of weld and component inspection on the shop floor, followed by UT when the business takes on structural or pressure work that demands volumetric inspection. Inspection contractors that chase pipeline and plant outage work usually add RT and then PAUT. If you want a Level III to sanity-check which sequence suits your work, book a Level III consultation.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Iowa, step by step

Under SNT-TC-1A there is no state NDT licence and no central certificate issued by ASNT for Level I and II. Certification is granted by your employer, following its own written practice. This is the path an Iowa technician follows:

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer must have a written practice that states how it trains, examines and certifies NDT personnel for each method and level. If your company does not have one, that is the first job. See written practice development.
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete the classroom hours your written practice requires for the method and level. Atlantis delivers these live online or onsite. For the hours recommended by SNT-TC-1A, use our training requirements matrix rather than relying on figures quoted elsewhere.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log documented experience in the method under the supervision of qualified personnel, at your employer's shop or on its job sites. The matrix shows the recommended minimums; your written practice may require more.
  4. General examination. A written test on the principles of the method.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on the equipment, procedures, codes and specifications your employer actually uses, for example AWS D1.5 for a bridge fabricator or ASME Section V for a pressure vessel shop.
  6. Practical examination. A hands-on test on real specimens containing real discontinuities, graded by a Level III or a designated examiner.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast checks, repeated at least annually as your written practice specifies.
  8. Certification. Your employer's Level III reviews the record and the employer certifies you. The certification stays with that employer.
  9. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets, you are recertified based on continued satisfactory performance or re-examination.

More on the framework itself is on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Iowa crews

Iowa's geography makes delivery format the single biggest decision. Driving a crew from Council Bluffs to a classroom several states away costs a week of production plus travel, and the equipment they practise on may not match what they use at home. Atlantis offers three honest options:

  • Live online classroom. Instructor-led theory sessions with Q&A, suitable for the classroom component of every method and for Level III preparation. See online NDT training for how the sessions work.
  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-supervised session at your plant, shop or yard in Iowa, using your equipment, your procedures and your specimens. This suits manufacturers standing up in-house inspection and contractors with a group of trainees at once.
  • Blended. Theory online, practicals and examinations onsite. This is the most common choice for Iowa employers because it limits time away from the floor.

We schedule around your production and outage calendar. Generating stations and process plants in Iowa typically schedule maintenance outages in the shoulder seasons, when power demand is lower, and ethanol plants plan shutdowns around their own maintenance cycles. Agricultural equipment manufacturers have their own peak build periods. Tell us your quiet windows and we build the cohort around them. Ask about onsite training for your Iowa crew; cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Iowa

Iowa's NDT demand is broad rather than concentrated. These are the sectors that generate most of the work, along with the codes and rules that shape it.

Heavy equipment and agricultural machinery manufacturing

Iowa has one of the largest concentrations of agricultural and construction equipment manufacturing in the country, from large OEM plants to hundreds of fabrication and machining suppliers. Welded frames, booms, axles, hitches and castings are routinely checked with VT, MT and PT, and UT is used on critical welds and thick sections. Much of this work is to AWS D1.1 or to customer and OEM specifications, and supplier audits frequently ask to see the written practice and the certification records behind every inspector.

Ethanol, biodiesel and food processing

Iowa is the leading ethanol-producing state in the US, with plants spread across the rural north and west of the state. Each plant has storage tanks, pressure vessels, distillation equipment and process piping that need periodic inspection, typically to ASME Section VIII, ASME B31.3 and API 650 for tanks. UT thickness surveys, VT and PT on stainless welds are routine, and PAUT and ET appear during planned shutdowns. Food and grain processing plants add similar stainless-steel and pressure-equipment work.

Wind energy

Wind generates a larger share of Iowa's electricity than in almost any other state, and the supply chain around it creates NDT work in tower fabrication welding, flange and bolt inspection, and in-service inspection of towers and components. UT and MT dominate on steel structures.

Power generation

Coal, gas and nuclear sites across the state need boiler tube, heat exchanger, piping and structural inspections during outages. ET on condenser and heat exchanger tubing, UT thickness and weld inspection, and MT/PT on rotating equipment are all common. Nuclear work additionally follows ASME Section XI and the plant operator's own qualification requirements, which usually go beyond a basic SNT-TC-1A certification.

Pipelines

Interstate crude, natural gas and refined-product pipelines cross Iowa, and construction and integrity work brings RT and increasingly automated UT to API 1104. Pipeline operators also require operator qualification (OQ) under federal pipeline safety rules, which is separate from NDT certification.

Bridges and structural steel

Iowa has a very large bridge inventory, including major crossings on the Mississippi and Missouri rivers. Steel bridge fabrication and repair work follows AWS D1.5, with UT and MT on critical welds and VT throughout. Structural steel fabricators serving commercial construction work to AWS D1.1.

Radiography licensing in Iowa

Iowa is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the state radiation control programme rather than directly by the NRC. Iowa is also one of the states that runs its own radiation safety certification for industrial radiographers. Anyone using sources or radiation-producing equipment must meet the state's radiographer training, certification and on-the-job requirements, work under a licensed company with a radiation safety officer, and wear dosimetry. Atlantis RT courses teach the NDT method (technique, film and digital interpretation, codes); the state-required radiation safety training and certification is a separate requirement that must be satisfied through your employer's licensed programme. Always confirm current rules directly with the Iowa radiation control programme before a technician handles a source.

What Iowa employers typically ask for

  • SNT-TC-1A Level II in the method, with documented hours and exam records under a written practice.
  • Two or more methods for smaller shops and contractors (VT/MT/PT is a common base; UT is the most frequent add-on).
  • AWS D1.1 or D1.5 familiarity for structural and bridge work.
  • For pipeline work, API 1104 knowledge plus pipeline operator qualification.
  • Some customers also ask for a welding inspector credential such as AWS CWI; Atlantis does not deliver CWI training, but multi-method NDT certification complements it well.

For pay context, see our NDT salary guide; we do not quote local wage figures on city pages.

Level III services and written practices for Iowa NDT companies

Many Iowa manufacturers and small inspection companies do not employ a full-time Level III. Under SNT-TC-1A, that is acceptable as long as the employer designates an outside Level III to handle the responsibilities the written practice assigns: developing and approving procedures, preparing and grading examinations, and overseeing the certification programme. Atlantis provides that service.

  • Written practice development: a written practice tailored to your methods, levels and customer requirements. See written practice development.
  • Procedure writing: method procedures that reference the codes you actually work to, such as AWS D1.1, ASME Section V or API 1104.
  • Examination administration: general, specific and practical exams prepared and graded by a Level III.
  • Audit preparation: getting certification files ready for OEM supplier audits and customer quality reviews.
  • Corporate programmes: multi-person, multi-method training plans. See corporate NDT training.

For the full picture of how employer-based certification works, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification, then book a Level III consultation for your Iowa company.

Practise before the practical exam

The practical examination is where most candidates are least comfortable, especially technicians who have only seen a method in a classroom. Atlantis's Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For an Iowa trainee, the welding workshop and storage tank scenarios are closest to typical fabrication and ethanol plant work.

The simulator is for practice only. It builds familiarity with setups, scan patterns and indication recognition, but it does not replace hands-on training or the practical examination on real specimens with real discontinuities, which your written practice requires.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As Level III he oversees course content, examinations and the certification support we provide to employers, whether the session is online or onsite at your Iowa facility. Level III candidates can review our ASNT Level III training programme.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Iowa

How do I get NDT certified in Iowa?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, you are certified by your employer. You complete classroom training, gain documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice. Atlantis delivers the training and can act as the outside Level III.

Can I take NDT training online in Iowa?

Yes. Theory for every method we teach, and Level III preparation, can be taken as live online classes. Practical training and the practical exam still need real equipment and specimens, which we deliver onsite at your facility. See online NDT training.

Is there an NDT training centre in Iowa?

Atlantis does not operate a physical training centre in Iowa. We deliver training live online and onsite at your company's facility, which for most Iowa employers means less travel and training on the equipment your crew actually uses.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom hours and on-the-job experience for Level I and Level II, and an employer can require more. Our training requirements matrix lists the recommended figures by method and level. The experience requirement, not the classroom time, is usually what sets the overall timeline.

Do I need a license for radiography in Iowa?

Iowa is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography companies are licensed by the state, and individual radiographers must meet the state's radiation safety training and certification requirements before using sources or X-ray equipment. This is separate from, and in addition to, NDT certification in RT. Confirm current requirements with the Iowa radiation control programme.

What does NDT training cost in Iowa?

We do not publish prices. Cost depends on the method, level, number of trainees, and whether the training is online, onsite or blended. Request an Iowa training quote and we reply within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Iowa employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used NDT personnel qualification framework in US industry, and it is what most Iowa manufacturers, fabricators and inspection contractors work to. Because certification is employer-based, a new employer will review your records and may re-examine you before certifying you under its own written practice.

Which NDT method should I learn first in Iowa?

For manufacturing and fabrication, VT, MT and PT form a strong base. UT is the most valuable next step because structural, bridge and pressure work needs volumetric inspection. Contractors focused on pipelines and plant outages often prioritise RT and then PAUT.

Can you train our crew onsite in Des Moines, Cedar Rapids or the Quad Cities?

Yes. Onsite training is delivered at your facility anywhere in Iowa under ASNT Level III oversight, scheduled around your production and outage calendar. See corporate NDT training.

Does my company need a written practice before we can certify technicians?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A requires the employer to establish a written practice before certifying anyone. If you do not have one, Atlantis can develop it with you. See written practice development.

Do you offer ISO 9712 or CWI training in Iowa?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A based only. Some Iowa customers also ask for other credentials, and we are happy to explain how SNT-TC-1A certification fits alongside them, but we do not train to those schemes.

How do I prepare for the UT Level II exam?

Combine structured classroom training with practice questions and hands-on scanning. Our UT Level 2 practice questions help with the written exams, and the Practical NDT simulator helps with scan technique before your real practical.
